title: Minimax Late Eligible Effect Estimation with a Shared Unknown Continuation Curve
banked_reason: Delivered tier incremental < floor field; not salvageable within scope. Current math and decision panels pass with no findings; the full-horizon shared-mechanism benchmark remains narrow and finite reporting is impractical.
gap_reasons: The delivered result is a matched all-horizon frontier on the fixed one-dimensional shared-mechanism parent, with no deferred conjecture supplying its upper bound or converse; the matched-rate headline does not overstate the statements. The n^(-2/7) endpoint inherits classical passive mode-estimation geometry, so the contribution lies in the finite-horizon transition and its coupling to an independently varying payoff, rather than a new location-estimation theory ([Akhavan et al., 2024](https://jmlr.org/papers/v25/22-1396.html)). Its application significance remains confined to a prospective homogeneous benchmark, with no demonstrated transfer to history-dependent selective eligibility. The certified computation grows exponentially in the capped power, and the conservative radius supplies no demonstrated useful finite-sample intervals, limiting the practical sample-planning case and the projected paper score. The finite-sample proof also invokes lem:bernstein-classical without either a proof or a precise published theorem citation, leaving a routine but explicit documentation gap. proof_attempt_summary: Derived the matched root-risk and finite 90%-honest connected-length order min{(T−1)^(3/4)/sqrt(n), n^(−2/7)} on the unchanged shared-continuation parent, using capped first-visit attainers and original stopped-record converses. After exact publisher-source Bernstein attestation and a missing dependency-edge repair, the current math and decision panels pass without findings. The general review grades the restricted benchmark incremental below the field floor; no formalization stage or Lean verification was run.
tldr: A late eligible causal effect weights a free outcome contrast by a high power of an unknown continuation curve. Shared early encounters identify the curve even when terminal histories are exponentially scarce. On the exact one-dimensional \(C^{2,1}\) parent, minimax precision and globally honest connected-interval length both have order \(\min\{(T-1)^{3/4}/\sqrt n,n^{-2/7}\}\). A total observable capped first-visit estimator and interval attain the frontier with verified finite-sample risk and coverage at every horizon, and a full stopped-record converse covers all original-record procedures.
gap: Fixed-horizon eligible-effect inference, concentration-dependent exposure tilts and passive mode estimation provide separate tools. The inspected results do not characterize their joint statistical cost for a free causal payoff weighted by a shared unknown continuation curve over every horizon.
fill: Uniform normalized-power derivative bounds and finite-power testing alternatives connect a capped first-visit correction to the complete stopped likelihood. The construction question derives the final pilot, error budget and arithmetic rule rather than assuming nuisance quality or Gaussian calibration.
